findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the endpoint's datetime ordering key
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime and this raises TypeError whenever build_cursor processes a non-empty page. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via strftime before scaling. The optimized_pagination=true path therefore returns a 500 instead of audit-log results for authorized users.

findings.title: value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps back to datetimes
findings.body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged, unlike DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor which converts the millisecond timestamp to a timezone-aware datetime. BasePaginator.build_queryset then uses that raw numeric value as the bound in an extra() comparison against AuditLogEntry.datetime. Subsequent pages will compare/filter a datetime column against an integer timestamp, producing incorrect filtering or a database/type error, so even fixing get_item_key would not make multi-page optimized pagination return the correct rows.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises AssertionError, despite the comment claiming Django handles it
findings.body: The advanced-features branch does list(queryset[cursor.offset:stop]) with cursor.offset < 0, accompanied by the false claim that 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically.' Django QuerySet slicing explicitly raises AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported.' A crafted cursor such as 0:-1:0 supplied by an authorized admin therefore causes an unhandled 500. The same crash remains for negative offsets with is_prev cursors in the fallback branch at line 886 and in BasePaginator.get_result at line 184, which now clamps only non-prev cursors.

findings.title: New optimized pagination path is added without any tests
findings.body: This PR adds a user-controlled optimized_pagination branch, a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, and changes slicing behavior in the shared BasePaginator, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for first/next/prev pages over datetime-ordered audit logs, crafted negative-offset cursors, or the superuser/global-access gating. Such tests would have caught that the new paginator crashes on datetime keys and on negative offsets before merge.
